equivalents.note: The Tibetan line says there is no doubt (the tshom med) about birth and death, reading bisaṅkā as 'without doubt', where Munidatta speaks of one who has fear of death (maraṇādibhaya, cp.22.m5), as the Tibetan comment also does ('jigs pa'ang yod pa).

The Tibetan drops the privative and turns the line into a rhetorical question, 'why would they not grow old and die?' (rga dang 'chi bar cis mi 'gyur), for the Bengali 'they do not become ageless and deathless at all'.
The Tibetan plays las 'action' against the ablative particle las 'from' (skye las las, las las skye) and, like Munidatta, takes kāma as karman rather than 'desire'.
The Tibetan takes bhrāntyā in its root sense of wandering ('jig rten 'dir 'khyam zhing, 'this world wanders and'), the verb it uses for bhram- 'roam' in 5a and cp.22.m6, not as confusion ('khrul pa).
ngo bo nyid, which the Tibetan also uses for svabhāva, renders svarūpa in bhāvasvarūpa, 'the true nature of things' (dngos po'i ngo bo nyid).
In this segment rang bzhin renders both svarūpa (skye ba'i rang bzhin, 'the nature of arising') and, in the Advayasiddhi verse, svabhāva, so the Tibetan does not distinguish the two terms.

The Tibetan renders Munidatta's utpāda with skye ba, its word for the song's jāma 'birth', and the paired bhaṅga 'perishing' with 'chi ba 'death' (de la 'chi ba yang ma mthong), so in Tibetan the comment keeps the song's birth and death.
The comment renders rasāyana with gser 'gyur, 'turning to gold', rather than bcud len, the usual equivalent, which the verse line 4b sets beside it (gser 'gyur bcud len).
The Tibetan has bla ma'i lam thob nas, 'having obtained the guru's path', with no negative, where Munidatta's gurumārgālabdhatvāt gives as the reason that they have not obtained it.

The comment has 'the abode of the Thirty-three' (sum cu rtsa gsum gyi gnas) for Munidatta's tridaśaṃ devālayaṃ, giving the full count of the gods, while the verse line 5a has no word for tiasa at all.

questions: cp.22.5a tridasa: the Tibetan line (gang gi g.yo dang mi g.yor bcas par 'khyam) has no word for tiasa, so it does not decide between tridaśa and the glossary's alternative tṛṣā, 'thirst'; the equivalent is given from cp.22.m6 instead.

cp.22.m4 buddha: the match looks spurious. বুদ্ধ sits inside suptapravuddhe (supta-prabuddhe, 'asleep and awake') in the Sūtaka verse, which the Tibetan renders rmi lam dang ni rab sad, 'dream and full waking'; nothing there renders the term buddha, so no equivalent is given.
cp.22.m7 janma and karma: not entered separately, since the comment repeats the verse words skye ba and las (skye ba las las su ji ltar 'gyur; byed pa po dang las bral ba) already given for 2b-6a.

Not in the input list but apparently present: 3b maalem̐ 'dead' (the glossary's mrta, maela), Tibetan shi ba; 1b bandhābae 'binds' (bandhana), Tibetan 'ching bar byed. Left out because the matcher did not list them; the reviewer may want them added.

cp.22.m7: the Tibetan ends with chos nyid ('dharmatā'), which has nothing to match in Munidatta's Sanskrit (paramārthavid yogināṃ acintyo hi); it seems to carry over the song's dhāma (6b, chos). Not entered, because dharma is not listed for m7.
